content:
Today's the day, Hunger Games fans: Sunrise on the Reaping is officially out in movie theaters. The good news doesn't end there, though. If you're excited to add this prequel to your physical media library next to the other films, there's no need to wait for it to run its course in cinemas. The 4K steelbook, standard 4K, and Blu-ray are all up for preorder right now as well at select retailers. Plus, both Amazon and Walmart are even dropping their own exclusive steelbooks for it, so there's a couple different cover designs to choose from.

However, one thing to keep in mind is that, since these have gone up so early, they don't have a set release date yet nor any bonus features listed. Once these details are available, though, we'll give this piece an update.

To break down the steelbook covers, Amazon's features a white background with pops of color bursting from the middle, alongside the whole cast of characters. On the back, you've got flowers and foliage forming the outline of Haymitch's flint striker, which leads up to the heads of a serpent and mockingjay. Check it out below.

Walmart's steelbook, on the other hand, is a lot more colorful in general. This simply features Joseph Zada's young Haymitch on the front cover and Ralph Fiennes' Snow on the back cover, with golden flowers around their heads and a purple background. Have a closer look at it in the image below.

If you're hoping to check out the film in cinemas this weekend before jumping the gun on buying its physical copy, it's sure to be a thrilling watch. Writer Tara Bennett gave it an 8/10 in her IGN review, writing that it's "one of the strongest entries of the franchise because of its excellent performances, especially Joseph Zada’s compassionate turn as young Haymitch." That's great news for fans.

And if you're looking to buy more physical movies that aren't just preorders, Black Friday sales are here to help. We've gathered up some of the best Black Friday deals on 4K UHD and Blu-ray movies so far from the sale, so you can add some new watches to your physical media library this winter.
